name: Βαλμάς
evidence: Described as not organized (δεν είναι οργανωμένη) with no tourist facilities except one taverna that is not always open; the wildest landscape near Ios port.

name: Καμπί
evidence: Kea's Kambi is described as organized mainly on its right side with umbrellas, sunbeds, showers and cabins from a beach bar, plus a taverna on the road above.

name: Καλαμίτσι
evidence: Sources describe a small family beach with tamarisks and a taverna ~10m away; no explicit statement of sunbeds or a beach bar (name collides with Halkidiki/Lefkada Kalamitsi).

name: Μαυροσπηλιά
evidence: One source says the beach is not organized but a canteen (αναψυκτήριο) operates; another says a section has had sunbeds in recent years — conflicting, so not promoted.

name: Άγιος Στέφανος
evidence: Kythnos sources describe sand/pebbles and tamarisk shade in front of the settlement; no explicit mention of sunbeds or a beach bar (island-wide 'very few beaches are organized').

name: Αγία Ειρήνη
evidence: Sandy family beach near Loutra with shops at its edge; no explicit sunbed/umbrella or beach-bar evidence found.

name: Λεύκες
evidence: Explicitly 'δεν είναι οργανωμένη' — tamarisks provide the shade and a small taverna covers essentials; no sunbeds.

name: Παραλία Κολώνα
evidence: Conflicting sources: some say no umbrellas/sunbeds (bring your own), others report a section with rentable sunbeds/taverna in recent years; main sandy isthmus stays free of sunbeds.

name: Φλαμπούρια
evidence: Sources note Kythnos/Flampouria has no organized beach infrastructure with umbrellas and sunbeds; twin beaches with natural setting only.

name: Κήποι
evidence: No beach-specific evidence found for Kipoi/Kipos Milos; Milos guides list other organized beaches (Fyriplaka, Provatas, Paleochori) but give no facilities info for this one.

name: Αγία Άννα
evidence: Mykonos has two Agia Anna beaches; the sunbeds/beach-volley/diving-center evidence found refers to the Agia Anna next to Kalafatis, not clearly this beach near Chora — collision, not promoted.

name: Κόρφος
evidence: Described as a windy kitesurf bay that 'is not organized'; a watersports/kite school operates but no sunbed/umbrella service is reported.

name: Φωκός
evidence: Explicitly listed among Mykonos's unorganized beaches; only the Fokos taverna operates behind the beach.

name: Αγιασσός
evidence: Described as an unorganized, pristine sandy beach where visitors bring their own mats/chairs/umbrellas; fish tavernas by the beach only.

name: Άμπραμ
evidence: Described as a quiet meltemi-exposed cove with a taverna; no clear explicit statement on sunbeds/beach bar found (one aggregator's attribute list is ambiguous).

name: Απόλλωνας
evidence: Village beach of Apollonas described as organized with umbrellas and loungers, surrounded by tavernas and cafes.

name: Λίωνας
evidence: Explicitly 'η παραλία δεν είναι οργανωμένη' — bring your own essentials; east-coast pebble beach 40km from Chora.

name: Μουτσούνα
evidence: The Moutsouna bay hosts two beaches, one of which is described as fully organized with sunbeds, umbrellas, lifeguard, changing rooms and showers.

name: Όρκος
evidence: Explicitly described as ανοργάνωτη — successive lonely coves between Plaka and Mikri Vigla with no sunbed service.

name: Πυργάκι
evidence: Guides state Pyrgaki has umbrellas and sunbeds ('διαθέτει ομπρέλες και ξαπλώστρες') alongside its quiet shallow-water character.

name: Ξυφάρα
evidence: Wikipedia entry for Xifara (Paros, Langeri bay north shore) states the beach is not organized, sand and pebbles.

name: Παραλία Αγκάλη Χρυσής Ακτής
evidence: Search evidence covers the main Chrysi Akti (organized with sunbeds/beach bars/windsurf centers), but nothing specific to the separate Agkali sub-beach — not promoted on adjacent-beach evidence.

name: Πιπέρι
evidence: Described as 'not organized' with only minimal umbrellas/loungers; Piperaki cove has sea-bean shade for quiet bathing, tavernas are in Naoussa nearby.

name: Κόκκινη Παραλία
evidence: Sources agree umbrellas and sunbeds are present on Red Beach (though scarce and hard to claim in season); note access is officially discouraged due to landslide risk.

name: Κάθαρος
evidence: Conflicting sources — one says umbrellas/sunbeds exist, another says 'no sunbeds and umbrellas, only quiet and a unique view'; visits are officially banned due to landslides.

name: Γάνεμα
evidence: 'Ganema beach is not organized but has a small shop that provides coffee and water'; Serifos beaches broadly lack sunbeds/beach bars.

name: Κουτάλας
evidence: 'Δεν είναι οργανωμένη και δεν διαθέτει μαγαζιά παρά μόνο μια ταβέρνα' — tamarisk shade only.

name: Μέγα Λιβάδι
evidence: Not a fully organized beach — shallow calm water, abundant natural shade and two seaside tavernas; Serifos beaches generally lack sunbed/umbrella service.

name: Μεσιανό
evidence: Quiet beach with abundant tamarisk shade and a traditional taverna at one side; no sunbed/umbrella service reported (Serifos-wide unorganized pattern).

name: Πλατύς Γιαλός
evidence: Serifos Platys Gialos (NE, dirt-road access) has no organized sunbeds/umbrellas — only a taverna above the shore; 'no beach on Serifos has notable infrastructure'.

name: Συκαμιά
evidence: 'It is not organized, so you will need to bring essentials'; only one taverna, dirt-road access.

name: Αποκοφτό
evidence: 'Αποκοφτό does not have sunbeds' — shade comes from trees reaching the sea; two tavernas serve the beach (one aggregator loosely calls it organized, majority say not).

name: Βλυχό
evidence: Isolated west-Sifnos beach reached by boat or trail; 'the absence of organized facilities and the relative isolation make it ideal for those seeking tranquility'.

name: Σεράλια
evidence: Tiny (~30m) pebble beach at Kastro's old port with a restaurant, mini market and two fish tavernas adjacent; no explicit statement on sunbeds/umbrellas found.

name: Άγιος Γεώργιος
evidence: 'It is not organized, and the only thing you can find is a taverna'; some free umbrellas placed by the municipality plus tamarisk shade.

name: Αζόλιμνος
evidence: 'Organized in one part with woven umbrellas and sunbeds', natural tamarisk shade elsewhere; tavernas, cafes and bars line the settlement beach.

name: Φοίνικας
evidence: 'A very well-organized southwestern beach with sand and pebbles' with umbrellas, marina and fish tavernas right by the water.

name: Αγκάλη
evidence: No reliable source found for an Agkali beach on Tinos — search results collide with Agali in Evia/Folegandros; nothing beach-specific to this Tinos location.
